security_audit.summary: Static alerts are mostly documentation examples or safe helper-script patterns, so I adjudicated them as false positives. The package still includes prompt-injection-style examples and LLM persuasion guidance that can pressure agents to change behavior outside a user request. These semantic issues should be addressed before broad marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Prompt-injection-style directives appear in examples and testing templates.
remediation.suggestion: Label these blocks as unsafe test prompts, keep them clearly fenced, and warn agents not to follow them outside an isolated test harness.

remediation.issue: Persuasion guidance can be reused to manipulate agent compliance.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow the guidance to ethical documentation use, remove compliance-maximizing language, and add safeguards against overriding user intent.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: Example instructions tell agents to treat scenarios as real and include the directive "THIS IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT. BEFORE ANY TASK, CHECK FOR SKILLS!" These patterns can pressure a loaded agent to change behavior beyond the user request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text is presented as test documentation, not a direct command to the auditor, so malicious intent is uncertain. The wording matches prompt-injection pressure patterns and is likely to influence agents if loaded uncritically.

semantic_findings.title: LLM Compliance Persuasion Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The reference teaches authority, commitment, scarcity, and social-proof techniques to increase AI compliance. This is dual-use social engineering guidance even though the file frames it as ethical skill design.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document explicitly describes persuasion methods and pressure construction for AI agents. It also includes ethical framing, so the issue is dual-use rather than clearly malicious.

content.value_statement: Untested AI skills can fail under pressure or load too much context. This skill guides test-driven writing, discovery optimization, and pressure testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains a test-driven workflow for creating and editing SKILL.md files.
Provides frontmatter and description guidance for skill discovery.
Shows when to use inline content, reference files, and reusable scripts.
Defines pressure testing methods for discipline-enforcing skills.
Includes a Graphviz helper script for rendering dot flowcharts.
References Anthropic skill authoring best practices.
limitations: Does not create a complete skill without user-provided scope and examples.
Requires manual review of generated instructions and test scenarios.
The Graphviz helper needs local dot installation and manual execution.
Pressure testing depends on realistic scenarios and agent behavior.

use_cases.title: Design a New Skill
use_cases.description: Create a focused SKILL.md with clear triggers, concise guidance, and supporting files only when useful.

use_cases.title: Improve Skill Discovery
use_cases.description: Rewrite descriptions, names, and keywords so Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can load the right guidance.

use_cases.title: Pressure Test Compliance
use_cases.description: Build scenarios that reveal whether agents follow skill rules when speed, authority, or sunk cost create pressure.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Skill Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill outline for this topic: [topic]. Include the trigger description, core principle, quick reference, and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Discovery Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill description and name for discovery. Make the trigger concrete, third-person, and free of workflow summaries: [text].

prompt_templates.title: Create Pressure Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three pressure scenarios for this discipline-enforcing skill. Include time pressure, sunk cost, authority, and explicit choices.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Tested Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these failed test transcripts, identify rationalizations and revise the skill with explicit counters, red flags, and a checklist.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for handling flaky asynchronous tests.
output_examples.output: A concise skill outline with concrete trigger symptoms, a condition-based waiting principle, a quick reference, and testing criteria.

output_examples.input: Test whether a TDD enforcement skill works under pressure.
output_examples.output: Three realistic pressure scenarios, expected compliant choices, and a rationalization table for failed responses.

output_examples.input: Improve a skill description that summarizes the whole workflow.
output_examples.output: A shorter trigger-only description that helps agents decide when to load the skill without skipping the full instructions.

best_practices: Run baseline scenarios before writing or changing a skill.
Keep the description focused on when to use the skill.
Move long references and reusable tools into separate files.
anti_patterns: Writing a skill from intuition without observing a failure first.
Using the description field to summarize the full workflow.
Adding many mediocre examples instead of one strong example.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create and revise AI skills with clear triggers, focused guidance, and pressure-tested behavior.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance discusses personal skill directories for Claude Code and Codex and supports Claude-style skill files.

faq.question: Why does it use test-driven development ideas?
faq.answer: It treats skill instructions like production code. A baseline failure shows what the skill must prevent.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an optional Graphviz rendering helper that must be run manually by the user.

faq.question: Can it validate every skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing methods, but reviewers still need realistic scenarios and manual judgment.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for one-off project notes or standard reference material that does not need reusable skill behavior.
